mainEntity.name: Does using steroid cream on my skin affect dental implants?

acceptedAnswer.text: Topical steroid creams applied to the skin work primarily at the site of application. However, in cases of long-term use of moderate-to-potent preparations over large areas, a small degree of systemic absorption can occur. This may, in theory, have some influence on healing processes following implant placement. The degree of relevance depends on your individual circumstances, and your dental team will assess this as part of your treatment planning. Most people using standard topical steroids for skin conditions are not excluded from implant treatment.

mainEntity.name: Should I stop using my steroid cream before dental implant surgery?

acceptedAnswer.text: You should never stop or alter a prescribed medication without discussing this with the GP or healthcare professional who prescribed it. Your dental team will not ask you to discontinue a necessary medication without proper medical guidance. If your dental team has questions about your medication in the context of treatment planning, they will communicate with your prescribing clinician to find the most appropriate approach for your care.

mainEntity.name: Can I still have dental implants if I have eczema or psoriasis?

acceptedAnswer.text: Having eczema or psoriasis does not automatically mean you are unsuitable for dental implants. Many people with these skin conditions undergo implant treatment successfully. The key is ensuring your dental team has a full picture of your health and any medications you use, so that treatment can be planned appropriately for your individual circumstances. Suitability is always determined following a thorough clinical assessment.

mainEntity.name: Will my dental team ask about my skin condition before treating me?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. A comprehensive medical history review is a standard and essential part of dental implant consultation. Your dental team will ask about all medications and health conditions, including skin conditions and any topical treatments you use. Being open and detailed in your responses helps your dental team provide the safest and most appropriate care.

mainEntity.name: What signs after implant placement should I watch for?

acceptedAnswer.text: After dental implant placement, your dental team will provide you with detailed aftercare instructions. It is generally worth monitoring for signs such as prolonged swelling beyond the expected post-operative period, unusual pain that does not respond to recommended pain relief, signs of infection such as increased redness or discharge, or any other symptoms that concern you. If anything feels unusual, contact your dental practice promptly for guidance.

mainEntity.name: Is there anything I can do to support healing after dental implant surgery?

acceptedAnswer.text: There are several steps that may support healing following dental implant placement, including following your dental team's post-operative instructions carefully, maintaining excellent oral hygiene, avoiding smoking (which is known to significantly affect implant healing outcomes), eating a balanced diet, staying well hydrated, and attending all follow-up appointments. Your dental team will provide specific advice tailored to your circumstances. If you take topical steroids, continue to use them as directed unless your prescribing clinician advises otherwise. Understanding what to expect during implant recovery can also be helpful when preparing for treatment.
